content:
"""
title: Weather Tool
author: greg
version: 1.3
description: Real-time current weather, multi-day forecast, and air quality via Open-Meteo, for use with Native Function Calling. Converted from the earlier Weather_AQI_Filter.py inlet filter - the model itself now extracts the location and decides when to call each method, so the old regex-based location-extraction and weather-keyword-trigger logic from the filter version is no longer needed here. v1.1: added placeholder-phrase detection (e.g. "current location") so the model asking for weather without a real place name gets an honest prompt for a location instead of silently geocoding nonsense words to an unrelated real place. v1.2: added raw coordinate-pair detection (e.g. "40.7128, -74.0060") so real GPS coordinates from Open-WebUI's {{USER_LOCATION}} browser-geolocation variable are used directly instead of being sent through the forward-geocoding search (which only matches place names, not coordinates) and silently falling back to the default location. v1.3: added reverse geocoding (via BigDataCloud's free API) for coordinate-based lookups, so responses show a real place name (e.g. "your city") instead of the generic "your current location" - falls back to the generic label if the reverse lookup fails for any reason.
"""

import re
import requests
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        DEFAULT_LATITUDE: float = Field(
            default=40.7128,
            description="Fallback Latitude if geocoding fails to resolve a location (your city)",
        )
        DEFAULT_LONGITUDE: float = Field(
            default=-74.006,
            description="Fallback Longitude if geocoding fails to resolve a location (your city)",
        )
        DEFAULT_LOCATION_NAME: str = Field(
            default="your city",
            description="Fallback location name for display when geocoding fails",
        )

    # --- Full WMO weather interpretation code table -----------------------
    WMO_CODES = {
        0: "Clear sky",
        1: "Mainly clear",
        2: "Partly cloudy",
        3: "Overcast",
        45: "Fog",
        48: "Depositing rime fog",
        51: "Light drizzle",
        53: "Moderate drizzle",
        55: "Dense drizzle",
        56: "Light freezing drizzle",
        57: "Dense freezing drizzle",
        61: "Slight rain",
        63: "Moderate rain",
        65: "Heavy rain",
        66: "Light freezing rain",
        67: "Heavy freezing rain",
        71: "Slight snow fall",
        73: "Moderate snow fall",
        75: "Heavy snow fall",
        77: "Snow grains",
        80: "Slight rain showers",
        81: "Moderate rain showers",
        82: "Violent rain showers",
        85: "Slight snow showers",
        86: "Heavy snow showers",
        95: "Thunderstorm",
        96: "Thunderstorm with slight hail",
        99: "Thunderstorm with heavy hail",
    }

    # German exonyms -> the English name actually indexed by the geocoding
    # API. Many cities are named differently across languages (e.g. "Tokio"
    # is German for Tokyo), and the geocoder matches literal name strings,
    # not translations - so a plain search for "Tokio" only turns up actual
    # towns named "Tokio" (there's one in Nuevo León, Mexico, and one in
    # North Dakota) rather than Tokyo, Japan. Kept from the filter version
    # since the model may still pass through a German exonym verbatim.
    GERMAN_CITY_EXONYMS = {
        "tokio": "Tokyo",
        "rom": "Rome",
        "mailand": "Milan",
        "neapel": "Naples",
        "genf": "Geneva",
        "warschau": "Warsaw",
        "prag": "Prague",
        "moskau": "Moscow",
        "athen": "Athens",
        "peking": "Beijing",
        "kairo": "Cairo",
        "lissabon": "Lisbon",
        "wien": "Vienna",
        "brüssel": "Brussels",
        "bruessel": "Brussels",
        "kopenhagen": "Copenhagen",
        "florenz": "Florence",
        "venedig": "Venice",
        "bukarest": "Bucharest",
        "belgrad": "Belgrade",
        "havanna": "Havana",
        "singapur": "Singapore",
        "neu delhi": "New Delhi",
        "den haag": "The Hague",
    }

    # Phrases the model sometimes substitutes for a real place name when it
    # doesn't actually know the user's location, rather than asking. Several
    # of these (e.g. "current", "my", "hier") happen to geocode to real,
    # wrong, unrelated towns if passed through to the geocoder unchecked -
    # so they need to be caught explicitly here rather than relying on the
    # geocoder to fail cleanly on its own.
    PLACEHOLDER_PHRASES = {
        "current location",
        "my location",
        "here",
        "my area",
        "where i am",
        "this location",
        "local area",
        "aktueller standort",
        "mein standort",
        "hier",
        "meine gegend",
        "meine umgebung",
        "vor ort",
    }

    # Matches a raw "lat, lon" coordinate pair, e.g. "40.7128, -74.0060" or
    # "51.5074,-0.1278" - this is the format Open-WebUI's {{USER_LOCATION}}
    # browser-geolocation variable substitutes into the system prompt, and
    # the model passes it straight through as the location argument. These
    # need to be detected and used directly rather than sent through
    # _geocode_with_fallback, which only searches by place *name* and will
    # silently fail (and fall back to the default location) on a numeric
    # string like this.
    _COORD_PATTERN = re.compile(
        r"^\s*(-?\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*,\s*(-?\d{1,3}(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$"
    )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Callable tools
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def get_current_weather(self, location: str) -> str:
        """
        Get the current real-time weather conditions for a specific city or place.
        Use this whenever the user asks about current weather, temperature, or
        conditions somewhere right now.

        :param location: The city or place name to get weather for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.
        :return: A short description of the current condition, temperature, humidity, and wind for that location.
        """
        lat, lon, label = self._resolve_location(location)
        if lat is None:
            return self._location_error(location)

        try:
            w_url = (
                "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?"
                f"latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}"
                "&current=temperature_2m,relative_humidity_2m,apparent_temperature,weather_code,wind_speed_10m"
                "&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&wind_speed_unit=mph&timezone=auto"
            )
            w_resp = requests.get(w_url, timeout=5)
            current = w_resp.json().get("current", {})
            if not current:
                return f"Weather data unavailable for {label} right now."

            condition = self.WMO_CODES.get(current.get("weather_code"), "Unknown")

            return (
                f"Current weather in {label}: {condition}, {current.get('temperature_2m')}\u00b0F "
                f"(feels like {current.get('apparent_temperature')}\u00b0F), "
                f"humidity {current.get('relative_humidity_2m')}%, "
                f"wind {current.get('wind_speed_10m')} mph."
            )
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Error fetching weather for '{location}': {type(e).__name__}: {e}"

    def get_weather_forecast(self, location: str, days: int = 7) -> str:
        """
        Get the multi-day weather forecast for a specific city or place, including
        daily high/low temperature, condition, and chance of rain. Use this whenever
        the user asks about future weather - today, tomorrow, a specific day of the
        week, the weekend, or "the forecast" in general.

        :param location: The city or place name to get the forecast for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.
        :param days: Number of days to include, from 1 to 7. Defaults to 7 (the full available forecast).
        :return: A day-by-day forecast listing condition, high/low temperature, and rain probability.
        """
        lat, lon, label = self._resolve_location(location)
        if lat is None:
            return self._location_error(location)

        days = max(1, min(7, days))

        try:
            w_url = (
                "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?"
                f"latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}"
                "&daily=weather_code,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_probability_max"
                "&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&wind_speed_unit=mph&timezone=auto"
                f"&forecast_days={days}"
            )
            w_resp = requests.get(w_url, timeout=5)
            daily = w_resp.json().get("daily", {})
            dates = daily.get("time", [])
            if not dates:
                return f"Forecast data unavailable for {label} right now."

            max_temps = daily.get("temperature_2m_max", [])
            min_temps = daily.get("temperature_2m_min", [])
            precip_probs = daily.get("precipitation_probability_max", [])
            codes = daily.get("weather_code", [])

            lines = [f"{days}-day forecast for {label}:"]
            for i, d in enumerate(dates):
                cond = self.WMO_CODES.get(
                    codes[i] if i < len(codes) else None, "Unknown"
                )
                p_prob = precip_probs[i] if i < len(precip_probs) else "n/a"
                lines.append(
                    f"- {d}: {cond} | High: {max_temps[i]}\u00b0F | Low: {min_temps[i]}\u00b0F | "
                    f"Rain chance: {p_prob}%"
                )
            return "\n".join(lines)
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Error fetching forecast for '{location}': {type(e).__name__}: {e}"

    def get_air_quality(self, location: str) -> str:
        """
        Get the current air quality (US AQI, PM2.5, PM10) for a specific city or place.
        Use this whenever the user asks about air quality, AQI, smoke, smog, or particulate levels.

        :param location: The city or place name to get air quality for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.
        :return: The current US AQI value and category, plus PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations.
        """
        lat, lon, label = self._resolve_location(location)
        if lat is None:
            return self._location_error(location)

        try:
            url = (
                "https://air-quality-api.open-meteo.com/v1/air-quality?"
                f"latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&current=us_aqi,pm2_5,pm10&timezone=auto"
            )
            resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
            current = resp.json().get("current", {})
            aqi = current.get("us_aqi")
            if aqi is None:
                return f"Air quality data unavailable for {label} right now."

            return (
                f"Air quality in {label}: US AQI {aqi} ({self._aqi_category(aqi)}), "
                f"PM2.5 {current.get('pm2_5')} \u00b5g/m\u00b3, PM10 {current.get('pm10')} \u00b5g/m\u00b3."
            )
        except Exception as e:
            return (
                f"Error fetching air quality for '{location}': {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helpers
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _resolve_location(self, location: str):
        """Geocode a location string, falling back to the configured default
        if resolution fails entirely. Returns (lat, lon, label) or
        (None, None, None) if the location is empty or an unresolvable
        placeholder phrase (e.g. "current location")."""
        if not location or not location.strip():
            return None, None, None

        if location.strip().lower() in self.PLACEHOLDER_PHRASES:
            return None, None, None

        # Raw coordinates (e.g. from {{USER_LOCATION}}) - use directly,
        # skip forward-geocoding entirely since it only matches place names.
        # Try to resolve a real place name via reverse geocoding for a
        # nicer response label; fall back to a generic label if that fails.
        coord_match = self._COORD_PATTERN.match(location)
        if coord_match:
            lat, lon = float(coord_match.group(1)), float(coord_match.group(2))
            label = self._reverse_geocode(lat, lon) or "your current location"
            return lat, lon, label

        geo_result = self._geocode_with_fallback(location)
        if geo_result:
            lat = geo_result.get("latitude")
            lon = geo_result.get("longitude")
            name = geo_result.get("name", location)
            admin1 = geo_result.get("admin1", "")
            country = geo_result.get("country", "")
            label = f"{name}, {admin1 or country}".strip(", ")
            return lat, lon, label

        return (
            self.valves.DEFAULT_LATITUDE,
            self.valves.DEFAULT_LONGITUDE,
            f"{self.valves.DEFAULT_LOCATION_NAME} (defaulted - couldn't resolve '{location}')",
        )

    def _location_error(self, location: str) -> str:
        """Return an appropriate message depending on whether the model
        passed a placeholder phrase (should ask the user directly) or a
        real string that just failed to geocode (report as not found)."""
        if not location or location.strip().lower() in self.PLACEHOLDER_PHRASES:
            return (
                "I don't know your current location. Please tell me the city "
                "or place you'd like this for."
            )
        return f"Could not find a location matching '{location}'."

    def _reverse_geocode(self, lat: float, lon: float):
        """Look up a human-readable place name for raw coordinates via
        BigDataCloud's free reverse-geocoding API (no key required).
        Returns a "City, State/Country" string, or None if the lookup
        fails for any reason - callers should fall back to a generic
        label rather than fail the whole request over a cosmetic lookup."""
        try:
            url = (
                "https://api.bigdatacloud.net/data/reverse-geocode-client"
                f"?latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&localityLanguage=en"
            )
            resp = requests.get(url, timeout=3)
            if resp.status_code != 200:
                return None
            data = resp.json()
            city = data.get("city") or data.get("locality") or ""
            region = data.get("principalSubdivision") or ""
            country = data.get("countryName") or ""
            label = f"{city}, {region or country}".strip(", ")
            return label or None
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _geocode_with_fallback(self, phrase: str):
        """Try geocoding the full phrase, then progressively drop the last
        word (e.g. leftover words that aren't part of the place name) until
        a match is found or nothing is left.

        Requests several candidates per attempt (not just the top one) and
        picks the most populous, since many world cities share a name with
        obscure small towns (e.g. "Tokio" is both Tokyo, Japan and a
        village in North Dakota) - the API's default ordering isn't
        reliably population-weighted, so trusting result #1 blindly can
        silently return the wrong place.
        """
        lower = phrase.strip().lower()
        if lower in self.GERMAN_CITY_EXONYMS:
            phrase = self.GERMAN_CITY_EXONYMS[lower]

        words = phrase.strip().split()
        while words:
            candidate = " ".join(words)
            geo_url = (
                "https://geocoding-api.open-meteo.com/v1/search"
                f"?name={requests.utils.quote(candidate)}&count=10&language=en"
            )
            try:
                geo_resp = requests.get(geo_url, timeout=3)
                if geo_resp.status_code == 200:
                    results = geo_resp.json().get("results", [])
                    if results:
                        return max(results, key=lambda r: r.get("population") or 0)
            except Exception:
                pass
            words = words[:-1]  # drop last word and retry
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def _aqi_category(aqi) -> str:
        if aqi is None:
            return "Unknown"
        if aqi <= 50:
            return "Good"
        if aqi <= 100:
            return "Moderate"
        if aqi <= 150:
            return "Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups"
        if aqi <= 200:
            return "Unhealthy"
        if aqi <= 300:
            return "Very Unhealthy"
        return "Hazardous"

specs.name: get_air_quality
specs.description:
Get the current air quality (US AQI, PM2.5, PM10) for a specific city or place.
Use this whenever the user asks about air quality, AQI, smoke, smog, or particulate levels.

location.description: The city or place name to get air quality for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.

specs.name: get_current_weather
specs.description:
Get the current real-time weather conditions for a specific city or place.
Use this whenever the user asks about current weather, temperature, or
conditions somewhere right now.

location.description: The city or place name to get weather for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.

specs.name: get_weather_forecast
specs.description:
Get the multi-day weather forecast for a specific city or place, including
daily high/low temperature, condition, and chance of rain. Use this whenever
the user asks about future weather - today, tomorrow, a specific day of the
week, the weekend, or "the forecast" in general.

location.description: The city or place name to get the forecast for, e.g. "Paris" or "Reedsburg, WI". Raw "lat, lon" coordinates (e.g. from the user's real-time browser location) are also accepted.

days.description: Number of days to include, from 1 to 7. Defaults to 7 (the full available forecast).
